arms.label: A5 — the shipped path: applicability, findings, the BA's questions and the refresh

configuration.searcher: production BM25 options (createInMemoryBM25) over rule id + summary, standing in for governingIndexRetriever
configuration.applicability: decideApplicability, rules with production's source line
configuration.questions: openGoverningPairs + openFindingPairs + buildGoverningQuestions: production's question text
configuration.answers: a question linking a rule with a baAnswer is given that answer; rejudgeAnswered + answersForApplyingPairs + applySettlements; findings produced again when a settlement applied
configuration.reading: readFindings: status as verdict, the verified clause as citation

codePath: governing/findings-store.ts findingPairsOf + governing/findings.ts evaluateRequirementFindings (the refresh after an answer)

citation.excerpt: Standard: Access control. Implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain electronic protected health information to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted access rights as specified in § 164.308(a)(4). [45 CFR 164.312(a)(1)]

judgements.businessFact: Does the cross-patient data issue cause a user to see or act on records of patients they have not been granted access to?

citation.excerpt: Implement a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic protected health information. [45 CFR 164.312(a)(2)(iv)]

judgements.businessFact: Do the backups contain electronic protected health information (patient records), and must authorized staff be able to decrypt them for restore?

citation.excerpt: Implement electronic procedures that terminate an electronic session after a predetermined time of inactivity. [45 CFR 164.312(a)(2)(iii)]

judgements.businessFact: What predetermined period of inactivity ends a session today, and is that timeout enforced on the server so the session is terminated, not just hidden from the screen?

citation.excerpt: The inactivity timeout SHOULD be no more than 1 hour. [SP 800-63B-4, Authentication Assurance Level 2, Reauthentication]

judgements.businessFact: What are the configured inactivity timeout and overall session lifetime, and are they at most 1 hour and 24 hours respectively?

citation.excerpt: When either timeout expires, the session SHALL be terminated.

judgements.businessFact: Does the background-services polling count as session activity that resets the inactivity timer, and will the session be terminated when either the inactivity or the overall timeout expires?

citation.excerpt: Unique user identification (Required). Assign a unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity. [45 CFR 164.312(a)(2)(i)]

judgements.businessFact: Does the merge tool log need to identify users by an individual unique user ID, or could users share accounts today?

citation.excerpt: Implement hardware, software, and/or procedural mechanisms that record and examine activity in information systems that contain or use electronic protected health information. [45 CFR 164.312(b)]

Implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain electronic protected health information to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted access rights as specified in § 164.308(a)(4). [45 CFR 164.312(a)(1)]

Unless otherwise specified in the description of a given authenticator, the verifier SHALL limit consecutive failed authentication attempts using a specific authenticator on a single subscriber account to no more than 100 by disabling that authenticator. … Authenticators that have been disabled SHALL be required to rebind to the subscriber account … to be usable in the future. [SP 800-63B-4, Rate Limiting (Throttling)]
Verifiers and CSPs SHALL use approved encryption and an authenticated protected channel when requesting passwords. [SP 800-63B-4, Password Verifiers]

judgements.businessFact: In development installations, will the login screen always refuse HTTP requests, or may it accept logins (password entry) over plain HTTP?

citation.excerpt: Following authentication, authenticated sessions SHALL NOT fall back to an insecure transport (e.g., from https to http). [SP 800-63B-4, Session Bindings]

judgements.businessFact: For development installations, will HTTP requests to the login screen be rejected, or will session cookies be issued so users can sign in and hold a session over HTTP?

citation.excerpt: Procedures for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords. [45 CFR 164.308(a)(5)(ii)(D)]

judgements.businessFact: Must the new user change the emailed initial password at first login, and how will the generated password be protected (for example single-use or expiring, and not stored in plain text)?

citation.excerpt: Passwords SHALL either be chosen by the subscriber or assigned randomly by the CSP. [SP 800-63B-4, Password Authenticators]
Procedures for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords. [45 CFR 164.308(a)(5)(ii)(D)]

judgements.businessFact: Is the admin-forced reset documented as a procedure covering who may trigger it, how the user creates the new password, and how the password is safeguarded during the reset?

citation.excerpt: However, verifiers SHALL force a change if there is evidence that the authenticator has been compromised. [SP 800-63B-4, Password Verifiers]

judgements.businessFact: Will the forced reset be used only when there is evidence of compromise or other event-driven need, and never on a periodic or scheduled basis for all users?

citation.excerpt: At AAL2, authentication SHALL use either a multi-factor authenticator or a combination of two separate authentication factors. [SP 800-63B-4, Authentication Assurance Level 2, Permitted Authenticator Types]

judgements.businessFact: Is a second factor (such as TOTP) mandatory for every user at sign-in, or can MFA be optional, disabled or bypassed for some users or accounts?

citation.excerpt: Assign a unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity. [45 CFR 164.312(a)(2)(i)]

judgements.businessFact: Will every person log in through the auth provider with their own individual account and unique identifier, which OpenEMR maps to a single OpenEMR user for tracking, with no shared or generic accounts?

citation.excerpt: Implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to electronic protected health information is the one claimed. [45 CFR 164.312(d)]

judgements.businessFact: How will the auth provider verify that each user is who they claim to be (for example, password plus multi-factor authentication), and will OpenEMR accept only successful authentications from that provider?

citation.excerpt: Implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to electronic protected health information is the one claimed. [45 CFR 164.312(d)]
Procedures for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords. [45 CFR 164.308(a)(5)(ii)(D)]

judgements.businessFact: What safeguards will apply to the password change on the login screen, such as password hashing in storage, strength rules, rate limiting and an audit record of each change?

citation.excerpt: When processing a request to establish or change a password, verifiers SHALL compare the prospective secret against a blocklist that contains known commonly used, expected, or compromised passwords. [SP 800-63B-4, Password Verifiers]
Procedures for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords. [45 CFR 164.308(a)(5)(ii)(D)]
Verifiers and CSPs SHALL require passwords that are used as a single-factor authentication mechanism to be a minimum of 15 characters in length.

judgements.businessFact: Are passwords ever the only authentication factor for OpenEMR logins, or is a second factor always required alongside them?

citation.excerpt: Implement a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic protected health information. [45 CFR 164.312(a)(2)(iv)]

judgements.businessFact: Will the sent fax details and any fax content stored in oe_faxsms_queue be encrypted at rest, and decrypted only when an authorized user views or forwards them, using the same mechanism as received faxes?

judgements.businessFact: Is a portal session terminated on the server when either the inactivity timeout or the absolute timeout expires, and does patient activity (including these AJAX requests) reset the inactivity timer?
